Commentary.Commentary: The inevitable has happened. The match has been called off. Once it started raining, puddles started to form on the ground and it never looked like the game will resume any further. That is it then! Join us for the second match on the 15th of this month at 12.45 pm IST (7.15 am GMT). Till then, goodbye and cheers!
Update - 1707 IST (1138 GMT) - IT has got a little brighter but there is a lot of water on the outfield, chances of resumption anytime soon looks bleak.
Update - 1518 IST (0948 GMT) - IT IS ABSOLUTELY POURING! Not good signs. There are puddles on the outfield too. We continue to wait.
Well, the heavens have opened up and we are in for a delay. The covers are on too. It's got quite gloomy Bere. We might be in for a lengthy delay.
OUT! TIMBER! Hume strikes. Breaks the stand that was starting to buld. Length and around off, this lands and jags back in. Mandade looks to defend but misses and it hits the stumps.

Toss - IRELAND HAVE WON THE TOSS AND ELECTED TO FIELD!

After an exciting T20I series it is now time for the ODIs. It was Ireland who bagged the previous series and we believe they are favourites heading into the 50-ocer format too. Zimbabwe will be without Williams and Ervine but Raza is back. However, it is still a very inexperienced side. This though should be a cracker of a game. Stay tuned.
... MATCH DAY ...

The stage is set for the first ODI which will be played between Zimbabwe and Ireland. The venue for this clash will be the Harare Sports Club in Harare. Ireland is off to a strong start on this tour as they have won the T20I series by winning the last two games. In ODI's they have faced a loss against England. The Irish have built a strong squad for this tour. Paul Stirling will be at the helm of the squad with the likes of Andy Balbirnie, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Andy McBrine, Craig Young, and Joshua Little to support him. They will hope to win the ODI series as well and return home with a dominant performance. Zimbabwe, on the other hand, has not been at its best for a while. They lost the T20I series at home and they also faced two consecutive losses in July, that is when they played their last game in the 50-over format. This will be a crucial series for Zimbabwe and they will give it their all to make full use of the home advantage and start off with a win. Which team are you supporting?
